This is part 3 of xboing-yeuw, and it was one command. The repo had been
enabled before the trailer-hook feature existed and enable — documented
as idempotent, "re-running is the upgrade path" — had not been re-run.
"Chained" confirms ethos coexists with beads' hooks rather than
contending for the single-valued core.hooksPath.

ethos doctor moves accordingly:

  Audit seal hook        not enabled here        -> chained seal section active
  Seal hook currency     no section installed    -> matches this ethos build (e7cacc3c)
  Trailer hook currency  no section installed    -> matches this ethos build (73b3300a)
  Local extension files  WARN no gitignore rule  -> PASS ignored and untracked

CLAUDE.md is 142 lines after the import — inside the 200-line budget in
.claude/rules/claude-md.md.

PART 2 IS STILL BROKEN, and this commit is the evidence.

Mission m-2026-09-06-009 is open while this is being committed, and its
create still emitted "binding mission: no session in context --
active-mission sidecar not updated". `ethos hook commit-trailers` — the
exact call the new hook makes — exits 0 printing nothing. Two
active-mission sidecars exist across 133 session directories, holding
m-2026-09-02-006 and m-2026-08-30-014; neither is this session's mission.

The hook is explicit that it will not guess: "No resolvable session, no
ethos on PATH, or no active mission means no trailer." So this commit is
predicted to carry NO Mission: trailer despite being made under an open
mission with the hook installed and current. Verified after the fact and
recorded on xboing-yeuw either way.

A hook that installs cleanly and stamps nothing is the sixth instance of
this session's recurring shape — a control that reports healthy and does
not run. Worth noting the hook itself is well-built: it documents a prior
cross-session attribution bug (ethos-pobi) where it globbed session dirs
and took the newest, and it now resolves only the committing session. The
defect is upstream of it, in whatever should write the sidecar.

One thing to watch, flagged by enable itself: core.hooksPath puts hooks
inside the work tree, so the seal is written into a tracked file. That
means commits can modify .beads/hooks/pre-commit. Not yet observed;
recorded so it is not a surprise.
EOF

EMPIRICAL RESULT 2026-09-06: part 3 FIXED, part 2 CONFIRMED STILL BROKEN. The hook is installed and inert. Proven by a real commit, not inferred.

WHAT JIM DID: ran `ethos enable`. Output:
  hook:commit-msg  installed  .beads/hooks/commit-msg
  hook:pre-commit  chained    .beads/hooks/pre-commit
  plus vendored guide, enabled marker, gitignore rules, CLAUDE.md import.

ethos doctor moved as expected:
  Audit seal hook        "not enabled here"      -> "chained seal section active"
  Seal hook currency     "no section installed"  -> "matches this ethos build (e7cacc3c)"
  Trailer hook currency  "no section installed"  -> "matches this ethos build (73b3300a)"
  Local extension files  WARN no gitignore rule  -> PASS ignored and untracked

THE TEST. Mission m-2026-09-06-009 was opened specifically as the test vehicle,
then commit a1d7a04 was made on branch chore/ethos-enable while it was open,
with the hook installed and current.

RESULT: `git log -1 --format='%(trailers)'` returns EMPTY. No Mission: trailer.
No Delegation: trailer.

WHY, traced end to end:
  - Creating m-2026-09-06-009 emitted the same warning as all eight missions
    before it: "binding mission: no session in context -- active-mission
    sidecar not updated".
  - `ethos hook commit-trailers` — the exact call the installed hook makes —
    exits 0 printing NOTHING.
  - Sidecar census: 133 session directories, exactly TWO contain an
    active-mission file. They hold m-2026-09-02-006 and m-2026-08-30-014.
    Neither is this session's mission. Both are stale by days.
  - The hook is explicit and correct about refusing to guess: "No resolvable
    session, no ethos on PATH, or no active mission means no trailer. The hook
    never guesses."

So the chain breaks at the sidecar, upstream of the hook. Installing the hook
was necessary and is now done; it is not sufficient.

THE HOOK ITSELF IS WELL BUILT — the defect is not in it. Reading
.beads/hooks/commit-msg: it preserves a chained host hook's exit status so
chaining cannot mask a host failure; it gates on the enabled marker; it is
idempotent, scanning only the trailer block so a quoted "Mission: " in a body
cannot cause a false positive; it falls back from git-interpret-trailers to a
plain append on mktemp or mv failure rather than dropping the trailer; and it
deliberately does not suppress stderr because "a silently missing trailer is
the failure class this hook exists to prevent". It also documents a prior bug
(ethos-pobi) where it globbed every session directory and took the newest,
cross-attributing one session's mission to another session's commit — now
fixed to resolve only the committing session.

WHAT REMAINS: whatever should write ~/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/<id>/active-mission
on mission create is not doing so for Claude Code sessions in this repo. The
warning text names the mechanism — "active-mission sidecar not updated" — and
adds "a subsequent Agent() spawn may still attribute under a previous
MISSION_ID", which is the same root cause seen from the delegation side and
matches the 954 KB of "ad-hoc Agent spawn (no mission contract)" advisories in
hook-errors.log. That log records every properly-contracted mission spawn today
as ad-hoc.

This bead stays OPEN on part 2 alone. Part 3 is done and should not be redone.

SIDE EFFECTS OF ENABLE WORTH KNOWING, both flagged by enable itself:
1. core.hooksPath puts hooks inside the work tree, so the seal writes into
   TRACKED files. Observed immediately: commit a1d7a04 was staged as 8 files and
   landed as 20 (+1864 lines) — the pre-commit seal swept in nine
   missions/*/log-no-session-*.jsonl files and three sessions/*/audit-*.jsonl
   files. Not wrong, but surprising, and it means routine commits will carry
   audit artifacts the author did not stage.
2. Five warnings on that commit: "active session <id> has no live audit file in
   <path>; if it was deleted, unsealed lines were lost". Three name the deleted
   worktrees .claude/worktrees/slsa-provenance-restore. So removing a worktree
   with an active ethos session loses unsealed audit lines. Worth knowing before
   the next ExitWorktree --remove.
